one_liner: CUDA byte-wise rANS encoder/decoder at 250-410 GB/s on A100; open alternative to nvCOMP's proprietary ANS codec.
what_it_does: DietGPU compresses and decompresses batches of independent byte arrays entirely on an NVIDIA GPU with a byte-oriented rANS entropy coder, plus a float codec that rANS-codes the exponent byte of float16/bfloat16 tensors. The C++ API (dietgpu/ans/GpuANSCodec.h) takes raw device pointers in stride, pointer-array or split-size batch layouts, a StackDeviceMemory scratch allocator and a cudaStream_t; a PyTorch tensor API wraps the same kernels. It is not a drop-in for any CPU or nvCOMP API, and the archive format (magic 0xd00d) is its own.
how_it_is_fast: Input is split into 4 KiB blocks, each encoded by one warp as 32 interleaved rANS streams (one 31-bit state per lane, 16-bit renormalisation words). Lanes that need to emit or consume a word are compacted with __ballot_sync plus __popc on the lane mask, so a warp writes a dense output stream without serialising. Encoding replaces the division by pdf with constant multiply-and-shift (state is capped below 2^31 to avoid overflow), decoding uses a shared-memory lookup table packing cdf, pdf and symbol into one 32-bit word, and histogram, table build, encode and output coalescing all run on device with no host synchronisation when scratch memory is pre-sized.
when_to_use: Compressing data already resident in GPU memory before sending it over NVLink, PCIe or InfiniBand, where interconnect bandwidth rather than ratio is the bottleneck.
Entropy-coding stage for a GPU compression pipeline (LZ or RLE literal/match streams) that needs an open-source rANS rather than proprietary nvCOMP ANS.
ML tensors in bfloat16 or float16 whose exponents carry about 2.7 bits of entropy, giving roughly 0.67x (bfloat16) or 0.85x (float16) size per the README.
Total inputs of at least about 512 KiB, ideally enough 4 KiB blocks to fill every SM; a batch size of 1 on large data performs best per the README.
when_not_to_use: Data whose redundancy lives above the byte level (text, structured records): byte-wise order-0 statistics compress it poorly; an LZ codec does better.
Small buffers under about 512 KiB, or any CPU-only or non-NVIDIA deployment.
Single arrays of 2 GiB or more: the ANS compressor fails a CHECK on rawSize <= INT32_MAX (issue #19, closed as not planned).
float32 or float64 tensors: the float codec supports only float16 and bfloat16 (float32 requests #11 and #15 never landed).
Projects that need upstream support: the repository was archived on 2026-06-14 and was labelled a very early alpha.

integration.dependencies: CUDA toolkit, glog and googletest (git submodules); the top-level CMake also configures the PyTorch wrapper, so find_package(Torch) must succeed even if only gpu_ans is wanted
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.10+, C++14 and CUDA C++14 (nvcc); a recent PyTorch build failed (issue #25, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118)
integration.platforms: NVIDIA GPUs only; README says CC 3.5+ should work but only V100/A100 were tested by the author (a third-party paper reports runs on H100)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; calls are stream-ordered and use a caller-owned StackDeviceMemory scratch object, so give each concurrent stream its own

gotchas: Inputs must be 4-byte aligned (kANSRequiredAlignment = 4), and the output buffer must be sized with getMaxCompressedSize(), which is larger than the input.
The compressed size is known only on the device; you copy the per-batch size array back to the host before you can move or trim the output.
Only probability precisions of 9, 10 or 11 bits are accepted (default 10); any other value hits a CHECK failure.
Decode trusts the stride you pass: a stride smaller than a member's compressed size can read out of bounds (header comment says it may segfault). The optional checksum is off by default.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick DietGPU over multians or Recoil when you need both a GPU encoder and decoder with per-array statistics (multians is decode-only), and over torch_ans when you want raw C++ device-pointer batches instead of PyTorch-only symbol tensors; for CPU entropy coding use hypersonic-rANS or htscodecs instead.
verified_claims_summary: The README reports first-party absolute rANS throughput of about 250-410 GB/s on one A100 at batch size 1 via the PyTorch API on torch.normal-derived data, with no baseline on the page. A third-party preprint (arXiv 2606.18900, seen only as a search snippet) measured 364.9 GB/s encode and 592.5 GB/s decode on H100 (256 MB, batch 4096 x 64 KB) against 480 GB/s for nvcomp-ANS; a 2025 user request for an nvCOMP comparison (issue #20) got no maintainer reply.
status_note: Archived on 2026-06-14 after a last commit on 2026-03-18 and labelled an early alpha; MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor, but the build is tied to PyTorch and nobody fixes issues any more.
